mappings.name: oauth token: the configured client credentials are accepted

file: Orange's OAuth2 client-credentials endpoint. It sits at the HOST
ROOT, not under /orange-money-webpay/{env} — that asymmetry is the
this file is what proves the derivation lands somewhere real.
Commentary goes in `metadata` because WireMock refuses a mapping
document with any field it does not recognise (a `//` key fails the
container at startup with MappingFileException); `metadata` is the
one field it accepts as free-form JSON and never interprets.
Priorities are explicit so the order of mappings in this file cannot
decide which one wins: 1 is the credential refusal, 5 (WireMock's
comment: The bearer every other Orange mapping implicitly expects. `expires_in`
is present, so the adapter caches it and the rest of a test's calls
cost one token request in total.
The bad-credentials case. `Credentials::Rejected` in the conformance
suite changes exactly one value — client_id becomes
`expired-client-id` — and the adapter sends it inside a Basic header,
so the match is on the base64 of `expired-client-id:`. Eighteen bytes
is exactly six base64 groups, so that prefix is stable whatever the
secret is: this says 'any request whose Basic client_id is
expired-client-id', not 'this one exact credential pair'.
401 on the TOKEN call rather than on the payment call is the
realistic shape: a rail that has revoked a partner never issues the
bearer in the first place. The adapter must turn it into
decline the merchant is told to retry.

jsonBody.description: Client credentials are expired or revoked
